summary: Duplicate record of us-tn-mount-cammerer: the same CCC stone lookout (1937-1939) in Great Smoky Mountains National Park, restored from 1995.

facts.design: two-story octagonal stone structure built from materials on the site; the 2014 state form says stone and timber
facts.status_note: The most recent visit account I read is from 2016; I could not confirm its condition after that.

staffing.status: not staffed; abandoned as a lookout

access.note: Reached on foot through the park, near the Appalachian Trail. I found no closure notice, but I did not read the park's current trail or tower notices.

visit.trail_note: Twenty hikers made an 11.4-mile round trip to the tower on a Friends of the Smokies classic hike in September 2016.

corrections.current: us-tn-mount-cammerer-2 is a separate tower record
corrections.why: Same tower: tnlandforms COT004 sits at 35.7635, -83.1613 and the NHLR entry at 35.763305, -83.161064; both are Mount Cammerer in Cocke County.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: tnlandforms lists 4928 feet (about 1502 m); the NHLR lists 4,845 feet (1,477 m). Not resolved here; the tnlandforms value is kept in this record.
The register says stone; the 2014 state form says octagonal stone-and-timber construction. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: This is the same tower as us-tn-mount-cammerer, and the story largely repeats its facts in new wording; the editor should merge or retire one record. The current condition after 2016 was not confirmed. The NHLR and tnlandforms elevations differ. Staffing as_of '1960s' is the register's phrasing, not a year.
